Class CausalStreams

java.lang.Object
io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalStreams
public final class CausalStreams extends Object
Builds a Topology around a single causal stage: one or more causal source topics feeding a CausalProcessors-decorated processor, forwarding to one or more sink topics.

This is the high-level, topology-owning entry point — it plays the same role as StreamsBuilder, but for a causal stage. It composes the low-level CausalProcessors decorator internally rather than reimplementing the causal engine; use CausalProcessors directly when you already own a multi-stage topology and only need the decorator for one process(...) call. Reach for CausalStreams instead whenever a stage needs a guarantee the decorator alone cannot provide, because they require owning the sinks: a uniform sink partitioner (CausalStreams.Builder.withPartitioner(StreamPartitioner)), co-partitioning validation that also covers sink topics (not just inputs), and a sink cleanup.policy check — both described on parsley.topology.validation. 

CausalQuiesce quiesce = CausalQuiesce.create();

Topology topology = CausalStreams.builder(userSupplier)
        .addBufferStore("parsley", CausalBufferLimit.ofDuration(limit))
        .addSource(CausalBuffer.of("prices", Serdes.String(), priceSerde))
        .addSource(CausalBuffer.of("orders", Serdes.String(), orderSerde))
        .addSink("enriched-sink", "enriched-output", Serdes.String(), enrichedSerde)
        .withPartitioner(tenantPrefixPartitioner)
        .withQuiesce(quiesce)
        .build();

KafkaStreams streams = new KafkaStreams(topology, props);
streams.start();

Runtime.getRuntime().addShutdownHook(new Thread(() -> {
    quiesce.requestQuiesce();
    while (!quiesce.isSafeToClose()) {
        Thread.sleep(100);
    }
    streams.close();
}));

See CausalProcessorSupplier for the causal guarantee and its preconditions — they apply unchanged here, restated in terms of what this builder owns:

  • Your key is your shard. Every source and sink this stage declares shares one partitioner (CausalStreams.Builder.withPartitioner(StreamPartitioner), default Kafka's own key-hash partitioner) so a shard never drifts onto different partitions across topics. That partitioner must read only the key, never the value — a protocol watermark carries no value.
  • Path integrity holds by construction. A stage this builder produces is exactly sources → one causal-decorated processor → sinks; there is no method that inserts a plain, non-Parsley node in between, so a hop that would silently drop the causal-dependencies header or swallow a non-emitting invocation without a watermark cannot be constructed through this API.
